item.title: The Resource Bill of Remote Video Transmission: Bitrate, Latency, Loss, and Three Amplifiers
item.description: The previous post, rescuing picture quality on a weak network, asked what receiving-side compute can salvage after the network wrecks the picture. This one steps back a stage and asks about transmission itself: what does it cost in bandwidth, compute, power, storage, and money to move a video from A to B. Protocol mechanics stay out of scope; where the groundwork matters, I point to the earlier streaming protocols survey and video compression fundamentals in this series.
